text:
Barrett Hayton's season is a good example of why we split process from results. With him on the ice at five on five, Utah has taken 64% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, and he's 10 points better than his teammates by that share. Those are strong numbers for a third-line center playing under 15 minutes.

The goals haven't come. He has two on 4.4 expected, a 5.4% shooting rate against about 11% our numbers expect from him, and his only goal in the last ten was the equalizer against Ottawa on November 7. That kind of gap tends to close when the chances keep arriving, and they have.

Evolving-Hockey had his value last season coming mostly from defense: opponents got 0.12 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, 89th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he gets plenty of shots off passes across the slot. He's doing the hard parts. The finish is the piece missing.
headline: Hayton is getting the looks, not the goals
